stem:
Asparagine and aspartic acid are two naturally occurring amino acids. Their structures and isoelectric points are shown in Table 8.1.

Table 8.1

| amino acid | structure | isoelectric point |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| asparagine | $\text{HOOCCH(NH}_2\text{)CH}_2\text{CONH}_2$ | 5.41 |
| aspartic acid | $\text{HOOCCH(NH}_2\text{)CH}_2\text{COOH}$ | 2.77 |

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Draw the structures of asparagine and aspartic acid at $\text{pH}2$.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (c)
(d)(i)
parts.stem: Propanedioic acid, $\text{HOOCCH}_2\text{COOH}$, is treated with an excess of thionyl chloride, $\text{SOCl}_2$. Propanedioyl chloride, $\text{ClOCCH}_2\text{COCl}$, is formed.
parts.text: Write an equation for this reaction.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
Propanedioyl chloride reacts with an excess of asparagine to form compound **G** with molecular formula $\text{C}_{11}\text{H}_{16}\text{N}_4\text{O}_8$.

Each molecule of compound **G** has four amide groups.

Draw the structure of compound **G**.

{{figure:pdf_visual_03.png}}

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Asparagine is hydrolysed with an excess of hot $\text{NaOH(aq)}$.

Draw the structure of the organic product of this reaction.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
A polymer can form from asparagine, $\text{HOOCCH(NH}_2\text{)CH}_2\text{CONH}_2$, as the only monomer.

Draw a length of the polymer chain containing **three** monomer residues.

Clearly label the repeat unit of the polymer on your diagram.

parts.label: (g)(i)
parts.stem: Aspartic acid exists in two optically active forms.
parts.text:
Plane polarised light is passed through pure samples of these two optically active forms in solutions of the same concentration.

Describe **two** similarities and **one** difference in their effect on the plane polarised light.

parts.label: (g)(ii)
parts.text: Give the term used to describe a mixture of equal amounts of the two optically active forms.
